reasons: Lake identity record verifies case_name Stanford v. Texas, court U.S. Supreme Court, date_decided 1965-03-01, and year 1965.
Lake citations match the asserted official cite 379 U.S. 476, parallel cites 85 S. Ct. 506 and 13 L. Ed. 2d 431, and vendor cite 1965 U.S. LEXIS 2380.

defect.evidence_quote: We need not decide in the present case whether the description of the things to be seized would have been too generalized to pass constitutional muster, had the things been weapons, narcotics or “cases of whiskey.”
defect.problem: The holding is directionally supported but the clause saying a warrant authorizing seizure of all materials 'concerning' a subject is unconstitutional is too broad unless limited to expressive/literary materials seized for their ideas.
defect.proposed_fix: Narrow the second clause to warrants for books, papers, or other expressive/literary materials seized for the ideas they contain, using the case's actual subject-matter sweep.

reasons: The opinion supports the heightened particularity rule for books seized because of their ideas: the requirement is to be accorded the most scrupulous exactitude when the things are books and the basis for seizure is the ideas they contain.

The opinion condemned this warrant's sweep over literary material concerning the Communist Party of Texas, but expressly declined to decide whether comparable breadth would be invalid for weapons, narcotics, or cases of whiskey.
residual_risks: No separate lake holding field is present; support review relies on the cached opinion text and treatment scope note.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: When a warrant authorizes seizure of books and papers because of the ideas they contain, particularity must be applied with the most scrupulous exactitude; the warrant here, sweeping in literary materials concerning the Communist Party of Texas and its operations, was an unconstitutional general warrant.

reasons: The opinion is centrally about the Fourth Amendment requirement that warrants particularly describe the things to be seized.
The lake treatment scope note identifies Stanford as controlling on warrants for expressive materials demanding scrupulous particularity.
residual_risks: The disclosed files do not define the corpus role taxonomy for Progeny; the role is accepted as a topical placement under Particularity.
